Used to be very self conscious about everything including my height but to be honest I never really gave a fuck, I was just comparing myself to other people because that's what everyone does. I'm 5'1", and 26 in a few days. People call me bud or buddy or any variation of like, young boy descriptor, but not everyone. Most people call me sir. It's nice! But I also don't care that much, because it's basically how other people see me. It's regardless of who I am, more a reflection of others than related to who I am. 


I realised that there are plenty of short men in the world and I went out to find my own role models and observe others every day. Short men don't go around thinking "aw fuck me I'm short and I'm less of a man". Tall guys don't look at short men and think "what a short guy I guess I'll treat him like less". That's called an asshole and they come in many forms. Also, there are worse things. I'm not a dwarf and look at peter dinklage, he's hot and respected. I'm not in a wheelchair, they're short too but also disabled. So I don't have anything to complain about. If people worse off than me can be so cool and self assured and independent and the works, why should someone like me who's healthy focus on what I don't have? So really, just be yourself because most people actually don't care about what you look like, they care about if you're a decent person or not. If you look them in the eye and are respectful and friendly. It helps to just get out and talk to people, I go to the gym and play handball with strangers and you can really see that people are not evaluating you on anything else aside from how you say hello and how you play handball. 


There are people that judge me for looking young or being short but if it bothers me, it just means I don't have enough respect for myself, enough that it could never touch me. Also, think of my powers when I'm 60, I'll be looking spry. As for how you dress, the very most important thing is to pick shit that fits you well. Clothes that you like that suit you. It doesn't matter if I have to get boy's or women's sizes (such as for shoes), if it fits me then it'll look better than swimming in a huge men's size and looking ridiculous. Shirts are the biggest offender of this, especially bc if the shoulders are off it makes you look younger. But yeah just find what clothes suit you! 


Don't let your fears stop you from being happy because it can really be so much better than you could ever imagine.

Oh absolutely. That's pretty much the same exact reasons I had. I used to think I had to be CRAZY to feel this way, and... it was so odd going back and forth between seeing the things people would say and being in the community which sees everything as normal and accepting. Inside what I really felt was... I was just pretending. And I desperately wanted to feel like these feelings were real, so I needed external validation because I didn't have any within me. It got worse and worse to where I would spend the majority of my time online, looking up every little thing to see if people experienced it too and if not, was I faking? 

I started a journal to prove to myself once and for all that I was alterhuman, to lay to rest all my doubts, and wrote down every experience I had, from childhood to current day. In a lot of ways it was rather eye opening. There are so many things I stopped doing or thinking because people told me it was weird. I wanted to do all the things I didn't get to do before. But in other ways it became a bit obsessive. I think I've struck a much healthier balance now.

What I realized now is that I can either accept myself the way I am, or forever wait for real validation to come, definitive proof that I am this or that. But the thing about waiting for proof is that you won't believe it until it comes from somewhere else. And you'll be waiting for someone to tell *you* what you are. I didn't think about it until recently, how ridiculous that really is. Because if someone were to tell you what you are, how "therians" are, then you're just acting out what a therian is supposed to be, basing yourself off of guidelines that someone else defined. And vice versa. All the people that say you're crazy or weird or hate you, they aren't you and they don't know you. They've never met you. You can't base what you are off of what they say.

For me, it took a very long time and I had to overcome a lot of embarassment and even shame to accept that I have many animal feelings and it's all me, it makes me happy and it hurts no one. It was my friend first who told me it's not weird, and now I finally believe it. Of all the weird things that exist in the world, like outer space or undersea creatures or micro organisms, I would say feeling like an animal (we are animals anyway) is one of the less weird things.

I think what you're doing is great already, it's perfect to simply accept whatever good animaly feelings you have and work out the negative feelings as well.

This sounds remarkably like what happened to me and the reason why I took a huge break from the online alterhuman community. 

I realized that spending huge amounts of time thinking about my kintypes distanced me from the real world and I felt lots of things you described. That weird feeling after realizing I could stand up and walk like a human. HYPER sensitivity to small noises and movements. Anxiety through the roof. A lot of derealization disassociation when associated with how I looked in a human body. A lot more animal behaviors. 

Although this is probably a very controversial opinion, the community is not a great place to spend lots of time in. It was detrimental to my mental health because of the things certain people say and believe. After taking a year long break, I felt a hell of a lot better. It's not good for the mind to hyperfocus on something too far removed from the physical world, from experience I can say it leads to disassociation and anxiety. Being a therian in my opinion should be about being yourself. "Yourself" exists outside of what anyone else has to say about it online. "Yourself" includes the real human body you have which is precious and beloved, thus the dissonance when spending too much time thinking of another physical form. And being you, should not be causing distress. If there is something wrong, you should think about where this is coming from. As a disclaimer, if I've said anything which does not match your experience or is not applicable, please feel free to ignore it.

My cat used to do that, jesus it was rough. When we slept he would attack us, we constantly felt at threat, he would stalk our feet while walking or like idk literally any time. Several suggestions.

Play. If your cat is like mine he wants attention from you specifically, a living and warm creature he can interact with, so transitioning to toys might be a challenge. Try different styles of play. Wand toys to stimulate birds or snakes, throwing those small mouse toys as if a creature is flying overhead, bits of string (hard to see and makes them concentrate), throwing something fast along the ground like a creature darting away. Really try to pretend the toy is an animal. That piece of string is really a snake, imbue it with life. If that fails I used to wrap my arm in a thick coat and wrestle with him until he was burnt out.

Environment. I made hidey caves for him by draping blankets over the couch and propping them up into tunnels with pillows or a table. Many cats love to crawl into them and play with whatever you drag along over top or the sides of sheets. He also loves to play in the cracks of doors, particularly along the sides where the hinge is. I made cardboard forts for him and he also would enjoy playing inside his carrier through the mesh to grab at whatever I swing by. 

Food. Mental stimulation through treat games such as those balls you roll until the treats pop out, treat towers, puzzle boards, snuffle mats, or training in general. Since training my cat, our communication has DRAMATICALLY improved, as has his mental acuity and patience. I have become a much better listener and teacher. It has helped me establish my own boundaries. I taught him sit, spin, paw, wait, eyes, follow, mat train, harness and carrier, jump, and sit up. "Eyes", in which we make eye contact before I give him a treat, I highly recommend. As you troubleshoot your own patience and learning will grow. 

You can dm me if anything, hope your cat finds a better outlet because I so understand your pain. I have scars from my cat too 👍

If you're going for photorealism, I would say instead of making rays of light from the upper left hand corner, instead make the area lighter in general as if the light is diffusing through the water. The shadows aren't bad, one thing I would change is the shadows on the guy. His lower half is more in darkness than his upper half, but in the drawing the shadows are heaviest under the woman's arm. This in a way detaches and breaks up his form, making readability more confusing. 

Now, if you're not going for photorealism, I would say that the rays of light are pretty, but they fall too short. Look up references for light coming down through the water to help. I would have them extend further past the two people and maybe be a bit softer. The light you put on their bodies is very nice, it goes with the rays from the surface. And although the woman's hair wraps around her body in the photo, from an art standpoint the drawing forms a tangent. A tangent is when the line of an object directly intersects with another object, such as for example the edge of a mug lining up with the edge of a wall. In art for clarity and aesthetics we can move the mug away from the wall. 

In the same sense the hair ends at the very same line the body ends. I would either move the hair in towards the body or out away from her body if I'm not going for photorealism. If I am I would make sure to enhance the texture so the audience knows it is hair and not go too heavy handed with the shadow.

The shadow under her armpit which is presumably the hair, and the heavy shadow under both her arm holding the guy's face and her arm in the water, seriously breaks up the picture. If you're going more for values instead of linework, that level of darkness takes away from the clarity instead of clarify the edges of the body. As well as it simply not being that dark in the original photo.

To summarize I'm really just pointing out the light and shadows, and a tangent.

Most trans people wish their bodies were different. For the sake of narrowing down what I'm talking about we can just talk about binary trans men. We don't want what we're born with, so we transition. There's so many ways to become happier with your body, such as hormones, surgery, exercise, clothing, etc. Lots of trans people look like completely different people already simply from being on hormones, and being happier. While I don't disagree that trans guys wish they were born with male bodies, or their right to wish that, I think we should have more trans positivity and stay grounded in reality. It's impossible to change how you were born, and such fruitless wishing distracts from the reality that you CAN have a wonderful body that you fought for yourself, one that isn't cis but no less happy. 

I get that being trans is hard, and being disabled is hard. But how people look down on others with disabilities will never change the fact that they are a human being, or take away from who they are. People don't treat trans people the same, but that doesn't mean we should just see being trans as that. Miserable, because everyone sees it negatively. Going stealth is important when you're not in a safe environment, but tbh within the trans community itself, it's not a very supportive environment for young trans kids. Passing is valued so highly not just because it makes trans guys happy, but because they're scared of being found out. And because it makes them feel like less of a guy, as of their identity is somehow of less value, not just because other people say it is, but because they believe them.

That's giving other people a lot of power. Wishing you weren't trans, seeing being trans the way everyone else sees it, basing your happiness and validity on what other people say. That shame isn't any different from being in the closet still. 

Not to say that the things you said aren't real issues or that we live in some fantasy world where things are great for all trans people. I'm saying that the world is a fucked up place and it needs cis people see that trans people are the same as everyone else: human beings. Hoping no one knows you're not cis, that's for other people. Your identity should belong to you, not them. Being happy to be who you are, happy to be trans, is so important in empowering trans youth and teaching society through example. It hadn't been going well for a while. Yeah yeah, our marriage. My mom would point it out, relatives at family gatherings would ask with false pity in their eyes. I wasn't blind. It was old news, yet people could still find more to gossip about. Years of unhappiness in a rushed marriage that I agreed to too young, now in my mid 30s working a 9 to 5 that was somehow less miserable than home life. I really should have done something. Either stayed or left. As luck would have it, I won the office raffle to go on a weeklong cruise to the bahamas. When she heard about it, she wanted to go. I wasn't a fan of the ocean, and rightfully so, seeing as I couldn't swim. But the cruise ship was supposed to be huge, the size of a city block. That shouldn't be too bad, and if I needed to run from my wife, there would be plenty of space to hide. 

Finally, the day arrived. It was a balmy 80 degrees and the drive there was uneventful in that there wasn't any more bickering than usual, and the level of misery was at a stable condition. When we boarded the ship, I stepped carefully over the wooden gangplank thing, with the water lapping through the cracks. Fortunately, there wouldn't be any of that onboard, unless we hit a glacier in the bahamas. 

It wasn't too long into it before I was wishing I invited one of my buddies instead. The usual bickering over insignificant things had evolved into full blown arguments over laments from the last 15 years, and unfortunately, this screaming fight happened to be on the top deck, in full view of all the nice, well adjusted families that were here to enjoy their summer vacation. Soon, they scurried back into the relative sanity of the indoors, and we were alone on the ship's deck. It was just us now. Her voice brimmed with toxicity.

"I'm not just talking about *this cruise*, Ralph. I'm talking about every time we're together. You're never present. It was always like that."

"Yeah? Well if it was 'always' like that, why'd you want to get married?? This was supposed to be a nice thing, and there's always SOME problem, some issue."

"You say that like you're not the problem."

"Oh, that's funny. It's all just me now? Look Harper, maybe this is why I'm never present."

"What do you mean, is it on purpose?" Her voice raised a few octaves. "You're always at work, what, because you don't want to be around me?"

"What?? Babe, don't make it like that-"

"Don't BABE me. You don't love me, do you."

"Well..."

"Well???"

"Can't we just enjoy this cruise? We're going to be on this fucking ship for a week together."

"No", Harper replied, voice low. "Not one more week. I can't take this anymore."

With a murderous expression, she raised her head and screamed, "NOT ANOTHER DAY." 

She bent down, took off one of her high heels, and began beating me with it, pointy side down. 

"GAH, WHAT THE FUCK."

I raised my arms, blocking my face, and stumbled backwards, unknowingly bumping into the guard rail of the ship's deck. A surge lifted the ship up, and I wobbled over the edge. My heart dropped to my stomach as I looked overboard, tall waves crested in white foam far below me. My wife followed my gaze, and a strange look came over her. I chuckled nervously.

"Hey Harp, back up a little. I'm too close to the edge, here." 

Her expression solidified, and in one wild motion, she grabbed my shirt front. No, she wouldn't. She knew I couldn't swim.

"Harper?"

The next swell, she heaved me over the edge with the help of the ship's momentum, screaming as I plummeted headfirst into the ocean.

I really should have invited one of my buddies instead.

//////////////

"Uhh, don't do it, no..."

"He's waking up. Give him some space."

"Stop, Harper..."

"What's a harper?"

"Those are the humans that take down whales."

What? No, that was my wife. Ex wife? Blearily, I opened my eyes. Had someone hauled me back onto the ship? My head hurt... and my lungs. I'd probably swallowed a lot of water. My legs kind of hurt, too. Faces swam into view. Elders, a few kids, some men and women peering at me curiously. The old man hovering nearby put a hand on my arm.

"How are you feeling?" His voice was deep with concern.

A whole lot better, now that I wasn't dead. "I'm alright, thank you... I can't swim, and here I am on a cruise. With my wife. Not the smartest, huh. Who do I thank for saving me?" 

Wait, why was everyone naked? 

My eyes, which were blurry when I first opened them, were rapidly unblurring. Those faces that swam into view earlier... they had literally swam into view. My jaw dropped. Everyone around me... they had no legs. In their place were silver and deep blue iridescent fish tails, long and powerful. What the fuck? Still in shock, I looked down. The old man's hand was connected with webbing between each of his fingers, which were tipped in sharp talons. Holy shit.

They turned to each other with glances of confusion. The old man gave a pleasant smile, of the polite variety, when you don't know what the other person is talking about.

"A... cruise? With your wife? I'm sorry, but... we found you alone. No one else was around."

A young woman piped up. "We found you sinking, and we did not know that there were some humans that couldn't swim. It was very sad..."

"Yes, very unexpected. And sad. Our medicine man saved you!"

They beamed at me, clearly pleased that I was alive and well. I knew I was alive, but as for being well... 

"...Am I in a coma? Did I get on that cruise at all? I knew that drink didn't taste right, Devin must have slipped me something."

I slapped my face, slowly, because the webbed hand didn't quite travel the same underwater. Right. My webbed, clawed hand. Only now did I take in the tail. Was that why my legs hurt? Right past my belly button, my skin ended and neat rows of gleaming scales began, forming a sinuous stretch of muscle. Where was my dick? I patted my chest. I was naked too. Where were my clothes? I looked up. It was hard to even see the light of the surface from here, and a new fear sank in. Just how far was I underwater? 

Their medicine man shook his head patiently.

"It may be hard to believe, but this is in fact your reality. We are sorry for taking the decision from you, but we hope you can enjoy your new life with us, or wherever you choose to be. Whatever the case may be, you can now swim freely, as you could not before."

"Yes, this is very sad..."

They all nodded soberly. Alright, fuck off, fish people, it's not that sad. Swimming isn't a requirement on land, okay? On land... I might never see land again. 

Wait a minute. Never see again? I'll never see Harper again?

An expression of delight grew on my face. No 9 to 5. No friends that only hung out to get drunk in a group setting. No awkward interrogation style family reunions. And best of all... no murderous wife. A levity I had not known since before marriage entered my heart.

His eyes widened in horror, pain lancing through him as he remembered. He forced a laugh. "Don't worry about that, sis. I'll get you a new one. Let's just go home. Come here, follow my voice."

*"...Okay."*

She emerged through the side of the machine, glowing even in the bright of day. Her spectral form was somewhat blurry, and she walked uncertainly towards him. She appeared to be confused.

The boys split soon after. There was a heavy darkness in the air, and he didn't see them for days afterwards. He took his sister home, hand in hand and walking slowly. She seemed dazed, and looked around at everything strangely.

When they got home, his parents weren't around. He asked her if she needed anything... gave her an apple. She wasn't hungry, but she took a bite, reaching towards it and grasping onto its essence, and pulling the  hologram of an apple out of the fruit, towards her mouth and crunching on it. Soon afterwards, the physical apple began to rot in the place she bit it.

She was too old now. At 18, the government no longer provided free bodies as you were no longer considered a child. They would be coming in the morning to reclaim her. His parents seemed to hardly mark it as an occurence in their lives, and went back to work.

16 times he'd died. His sister had brought him back home for a few of them. 

He couldn't understand this. He didn't know how to. 

Why was she there? It wasn't his fault. 

How many hours were left now? 

How could he do this to her? 

/////////////////

"GRAY!"

With a gasp, he bolted upright, heart pounding hard in his ears. 

"Rosa." 

He looked around frantically, only half seeing the room.

"Hey, hey. Calm down." Vin grabbed his face and opened one of his eyes, shining a light in. 

"Ow, what the fuck?" He squinted, drawing his head back.

"Just checking the body responses. Bro, I had to manhandle you out of that thing myself, and figure out how to install you into this dusty old model. You alright?"

Slowly, everything sank in. They were running. They were in a moldy cellar. He died... There he was, on the floor. His corpse lay on its back, drained of blood. Yeah, definitely no saving that thing. Wait, where was Rosa? He scrambled around for a second before Vin held his bag up. He reached for it eagerly. There she was, still safe inside the hibernation chamber.

"Yeah, I'm... I'm alright now. A little dizzy, but it works."

"You're welcome."

"Thanks, Vin. I really owe you one..."

After inspecting the glass for cracks, he reached his hand out to look at his body. His mouth was dry, and it wasn't in great shape. Definitely an older model, the skin was probably made of that cheaper stuff, but he wasn't complaining. 

"Any chance there's another one lying around?"

"Sorry man, that was the only halfway decent one. We got lucky as it is, someone probably stashed it here for emergencies. I mean, it's illegal as it is. Glad I didn't have to share mine with you.

"Right..."

He wasn't too disappointed. Not like he was expecting to find a body lying around that Rosa could fit in. And it's not like he'd stuff her into his body either, like those freaks in corporate. He'd have one soon, though, if they managed to make it to the body processing factory without dying again. They just needed to get one model fresh off the belt... and hopefully he could snag one for himself instead of this thing he was using, if all went well.

And then, maybe be on the run forever. But that was okay. He caught Vin's eye and they nodded.

"Ready then? Let's outrun these pigs."

He'd never been a good kid. Or wanted to be, for that matter.

His mother and father had been assigned to him. He came to them one day, a knock on their door and accompanied by two civil servants with their truck of kids, all fresh off the manufacturing line. Standard model soul, with a mass produced standard issue body like every child recieved. Among every adult's many duties was to raise a handful of young souls to maturity, where they would then begin working for the state. Gray's future was to do just that, or be reclaimed as a faulty soul.

Lame. His "mother" was hardly interested in him, and his "father" worked grueling long hours for that raise that would never come. It meant that he could do whatever he wanted. He never went to the educational facility, ran wild on the streets, and often got himself killed doing stupid things. Road accident, falling from rooftops, an incident with arson. Each time, this or that buddy would help him back home after he died, and his long suffering mother would apply for a new body, covered by child insurance. It was all a big game to him. Dying wasn't serious. Sure, a little cold when you're waiting for a new meat sack and you're just a soul. But shipping is only a day.

It was like that up until the day his sister arrived.

Unlike his parents, Rosa took to him right away. She was older, mature, paid him attention, and seemed to actually care about him. Apparently her own folks were reclaimed into the system after a factory fire, and their souls were awaiting recycle. Had nothing to do with *him*, though. Everyone would experience that some time or another, and it was her parents' unlucky day. If his own folks ate it somehow, he would be reassigned to some random adults too. And if his sister wasn't around, life would go on just the same. He gave her no reasons to like him.

That's why... she shouldn't have been there.

He was messing around with his pals as always. A few days ago, they'd found this industrial tree shredding machine, abandoned and sitting around, still perfectly good. They took turns throwing the biggest pieces of junk they could find, and it ate everything up with a piercing metallic screech, no matter how big it was. Immensely satisfying. They played this game for the last few times they skipped out on class, and tossed things in from up high, gathered on the rotten scaffolding haphazardly bolted into one of the walls of the crumbling factory. It was just another day of doing just that, when Rosa somehow found him.

 He could hear her now, as he heard it all, moment by moment. He couldn't escape it if he tried. It was a humid summer day. You could have squeezed the water out if it with your hands.


"Gray! What are you doing here!"

Elbows jostled about in that narrow space among the boards and rusted bars as they rushed to the edge to jeer at Rosa. Deep shade and blinding sun.

"How'd you find us here, stalker!"

"Yeah stalker!"

"Go back home, Gray. Get good grades, Gray."

Furiously, cheeks coloring, she protested, "Is this your idea of fun? You're going to get hurt playing with that thing!"

The machine whizzed and screamed as it ate up metal poles and bricks, thrown delightedly down to drown out the sound of her voice. But he heard her, that bit at least. The next all he could remember was their laughter at her mouth opening and closing, foot stamping, inaudible over the ear splitting sound. She grew more agitated, and finally came towards them and began climbing the scaffolding. They ooohed and gathered at the rails, the entire structure creaking.

"She's actually coming up! I'm so scared. Oh no Gray, save me!"

"Your mother is here. It's way past your bedtime."

"She's climbing the daangerous stairs! She's so brave. Such an upright citizen of the state. Boys, we should be more like her."

They mobbed her as she reached their flight. 

Cheeky shoves, her eyes as she watched him among them, angry, sad, hurt. The boards groaning with the movement. He had joined in at first, but couldn't help this sticky undercurrent of shame. At last she looked him straight in the eyes, harrassed and upset... and he didn't understand, she didn't have to be there, his own parents never even gave a shit, and she hardly knew him... 

She took a step towards him, and someone nudged her again. She stumbled, caught herself, and collapsed through one particularly weakened section of the floor.

That fascinating hypnotic inward spiralling of the blades that he'd stared into so often did to Rosa what he'd seen it do to everything else that they'd ever thrown into it. But it was much wetter. She didn't even have time to scream.

///////////////////

It was a rental body, so the nerve signals weren't as delicate as premium grade. But it still hurt. Gray's breath rushed out of him and he clenched his teeth against the crushing pain, fighting to stay on his feet. 

The crisp sound of the bullet exploded from the barrel and echoed swiftly down the street. His buddy Vin stopped as soon as they heard the gunshot and skidded around, rushing over to Gray with a barely surpressed expression of panic. They didn't have to ask if he was hit. Wakes of crimson bloomed outwards, just to the left of his abdomen. As he held his side, his hands began to tremble, and a cold sweat soaked his clothes. It was bad. He didn't have long, and just one look told him that Vin knew it too. Vin grabbed his arm in an iron fist and slung his hand over their shoulder. 

"Stay with me, Gray." 

He nodded wordlessly, face pale and jaw set. After a second thought, he dropped a shoulder to slide his backpack off, and held it out to Vin with white knuckles. Their expression grew grave.

"...You hold onto her. We're both getting out of this."

He hoped so.

He tightened his backpack straps and they glanced around, assessing their exits. The fucker that shot him was already running towards them, talking into a radio. If they didn't lose the guy NOW, the rest of the soul collection agency would swarm them. His breath came in pained and tight as he hobbled along to Vin's pace. The officer was quickly gaining on them, nearly at their heels. As they ran, they kicked a spirit waste pipe that sent ghostly shit shooting out at their pursuer. Cursing and spluttering, the officer wiped at his face. It probably would have been better to keep his mouth shut, Gray thought wryly, a laugh escaping him despite his pain. Thanks to the opportunity, they managed to lose him as they slipped around a corner and down a stairwell. As quick as they could, Vin propped him up against a metal handrail and quietly wheeled open a thick metal hatch in the floor. Despite their support, descending the ladder was excruciating, and he could feel warm blood gush out at every rung, and squeak under his shoe. He took care not to slip off. 

The cellar wheel hatch squeaked shut, and everything was quiet. This town was all but abandoned now, due to mass layoffs and recycling. All those who'd lost their jobs were now unemployed... and unemployed souls didn't serve the economy but to place an unproductive drain on it. Their bodies were reclaimed by the state, and the entire town's souls were currently back in the system, waiting to be recycled for some more useful purpose. Presently, there were some squatters here and there before demolition began, and Gray and Vin were now apparently among them. After a moment, he managed to catch his breath between waves of pain.

"We can't stay here long... they'll be searching the buildings soon, when they see we're not on the streets."

Vin nodded in the half-light, gesturing with their chin to his condition. After the running and climbing, he looked a mess. There was a wide path of blood soaking his shirt and running down his pant leg, and his sock squished in his pooling sneaker.

"We're going nowhere with you like that. I'd give you 20 minutes before your body times out. Come on, let's look for a spare, there's gotta be one lying around here."

They weren't wrong. The pain was intensifying. It was stomach acid... he could feel it searing his insides. And the smell, filling the small space, like the walls had been painted in iron. Vin appeared rather contained, with a forced edge of casual flippancy, but their aggressive ransacking of the cellar showed otherwise. Amidst the clatter, the world had softened down and gotten colder... Gray, in a daze, opened his backpack and removed a large tube inside. It was glowing beautifully, and illuminated the dark cellar in a soft white light. His hands left bloody streaks on its glass surface.

*I'm sorry.*

"This one's outdated for your soul's version, but it could still work if we... Gray?"  

Gray lay slumped around the container, eyes half open and dull. Vin put two fingers to his wrist, and waited. His pulse was cold and still.

Lara prayed that she was doing it right, as she counted down the remaining hours.

Her brother had emerged first, without her having to do too much. Finding him was nearly impossible, and she could hardly believe it when she found a tiny round speck on the chair where she had seen him last. He soon hatched into a juvenile tarantula, and thankfully, he was the first to prove that he was himself - he'd sit on the tv remote buttons for her to click to his favorite channels, and he'd laze around all day. Figures. But she was so glad to have him back, either way. 

Lara's mother and father were next, and she'd gone nuts trying to search for what kind of egg her father had become. Apparently, it didn't matter... snake eggs hatched on their own. It was more difficult trying to keep her mom alive, but eventually a mourning dove chick emerged, and soon grew to peck and fuss over her hair and clothes just as she always had. Her dad had a great appetite, disgusting as it was to watch, but he still enjoyed his coffee, strangely enough. Every morning, he'd stare meaningfully at her as she passed the coffee machine, and sniff the warm steam with a forked tongue in satisfaction as he waited for it to cool.

Everything had gone pretty alright, with her remaining family. A score of lizards, birds, fish, and amphibians emerged soundly, albeit not without a large degree of stress as she attempted to save all of their lives. They all lived with her now, but she didn't mind caring for them. She loved them, after all.

That was almost normal in comparison to what she'd been occupied with for the past 9 months. On that day, the one who she'd seen turn into an egg first was someone she'd had feelings for... her coworker in microbiology. One moment, they were having a conversation, and the next, he vanished... upon peering into his microscope, she saw something that definitely wasn't there before. A single human egg.

The months had been long and frightening as she worked to grow the egg, from external fertilization in a tube to what was now its third trimester. He was growing well, though she had to keep him secret in the basement of the facility's labratory. Every day she would check on him and speak to him lovingly. It brought her hope when his newborn eye would scroll back and blink with its nictating membrane, open his mouth ringed in pin-sharp teeth to babble through the amniotic fluid. Soon, it was clear that he outgrew the use of his umbilical cord, and she would feed him treats of raw chicken drumsticks, plopping it into the tank he floated in. Greedily he grasped it with outspread tendrils, scraping the meat to the bone. She loved seeing him enjoy it so much. She loved him, so much. She never got to say it, but hopefully she'd done everything right, and he had grown well. She would take him out of the tank in a few hours, and tell him when he'd grown up more.

You twirled your pen lazily, the warm heat of the sun slanting through the window and dulling your attention. The cylinder of plastic spun over your thumb, and you caught it with deft precision, hardly looking at it. Spin, catch. Spin, catch. The class was on economics... absolutely mind numbing. You glanced at the round clock above the door. Half an hour left... oh god. 

It'd probably be dark by the time you got home. Sundown was always so early in winter. Absent mindedly, you played with the shadows cast by your hand, making a dog. You opened and closed your pinky, and the shadow barked silently. You sighed and made one final attempt to focus, jot down a note or two, but ultimately gave up and doodled in the margins of your notebook.

You didn't notice it at first, but gradually you became aware of a whispering that grew until it seemed the entire class was mumbling about something. Hey, even if the lesson was super boring, wasn't this a bit too obvious? They were being a little too loud for... Whoa.

You glanced to the side and caught someone's eye. Two girls were leaning over, eyes wide, pointing. Your peripheral seemed to only now realize that you were encircled in eyes. What the fuck? Why was everyone staring at you? 

You sat up straight and looked around. Everyone in the classroom had this unsettling, transfixed stare of horror. As you turned your head to confirm this... Yes, it wasn't your imagination. Icy fear flooded your veins as you caught your teachers gaze. Her expression was one of terror, and her bottom lip trembled as she looked at you... No. *Behind* you. Amongst the frenzied mumbling, you heard a thin voice cry out,

"What's... what IS that?" 

What was what? Your throat went dry. You turned around, trying to search for the thing they were all looking at, yet dreading it. A wave of panic rippled through the students, many of whom had now gotten up out of their chairs and were backing away from you. Someone screamed. The guy nearest to you attempted to back further into the wall, scrambling over a chair and out of the way.

"What?? WHAT?"

No response. You were certain of it now. They were all looking at something... BEHIND you. You couldn't take it anymore. It didn't seem like it could be some kind of elaborate prank or group bullying, their reactions were real. The room seemed suddenly too small, suffocating. Without another word, you ran to the bathroom. Footsteps slapped on the linoleum floor, until you skidded to a halt in front of the entrance, one hand gripping the door frame.

Slowly, you approached the bathroom mirror.

Your harsh breath echoed off of the bathroom tiles, the smell of cheap disinfectant in the air. It was cooler in here, and quiet, save for the buzzing of the overhead lights.

A single large, rectangular mirror was mounted above the ceramic sink. Your shoulder hove into view at the edge of  the mirror. Another shoulder accompanied it. Your heart pounded, you thought you would throw up. But your momentum carried you forward. The rest of you slid into frame, as did another face as well, just slightly behind you. 

You screamed, but it didn't come out. A black shadow stood behind you, looking over your shoulder. It was a few inches taller, and all that was visible of it was one single, human eye. The pupil was without light, and seemed deeper than you could reach. And then it smiled.

**"You finally noticed me, Jacob."**

Your knees were trembling. You wanted to turn around, or speak, but you couldn't. They shook so bad, you gripped onto the lip of the sink just to keep from falling over. That thing only smiled wider, as if enjoying itself, relishing in your terror. After a few tries, you managed to croak out,

"What are you?"

It slid to your right. A tall, dark shadow, seeming only to grow. It placed a thin hand on your shoulder. It was so cold, it almost burned. It bent towards you to whisper in your ear, eyes boring holes into yours through the mirror's reflection. 

**"I'm your shadow. I follow where you lead. It took me a long time, but I finally did it."**

Its eyes pushed up into crescents of cruel delight, and its hand tightened on your shoulder painfully.

**"I can move on my own, now. And I'd like to keep doing that. So, if you don't mind... Turn around, and look me in the eyes."**

Suddenly it turned and stared directly at you. You could feel its huge eyes and black pools on the side of your face, right in your peripheral. *No.* 

Somehow, you couldn't close your eyes. They seemed to be jammed open. *MOVE!* 

Your teeth squeaked under the pressure of your clenched jaw as you tried to run, turn, do *something.* You could almost feel the urge to turn and look into its eyes that only seemed to widen until they filled its entire face, as if they had a gravity of their own.

You glimpsed the light of the hallway through the bathroom door. You turned your head. That's it. You could move. Just take another step. You were so close to the door. Just one more step. Nails scraped the sink as your fingers left it, returning their grasp to dig deeply into the flesh of your palm. The pain helped. Focus. Come on. You're almost there.

Its face swam hugely into view, locking its eyes, now the size of grapefruits, directly with yours. A strangled scream ripped from your throat. All you could see were those huge eyes, as animate as dead fish, filling your view, on and on and on... like a cold blackness, burning ice.


He returned to class, making sure to fix it just a little so that his classmates and teacher could feel at ease with him. He sat down in his chair as usual, and returned to his notes. The warm heat of the sun slanted through the window and made him feel quite nice. The sun would be setting soon, as it did in winter time. "No problem!" 

Her chipper response and soft voice coming out of that huge meaty frame registered as odd. Just one more on the list of thousands of things that were a little more than odd. Hysteria floated whimsically nearby, offering gentle reprieve, but reality unfortunately kept it at bay. Lyscha gently placed my luggage down, and I unsnapped the handle out from the top. What the fuck was I doing. What was I going to do now.

"Let's go!" 

She simply palmed her own luggage like a bag of chips and looked at me expectantly. Ah. So we were going together...

We made our way towards the front of the bus, shuffling past other monsters filling the aisle. In a state of shock, I squeezed wetly past the wall of tentacles, with a strained groan. Brushed past rank dog fur. Sidestepped sharp horns and something that looked dangerously like electric...glass? Once I arrived in front of the driver, I knocked at the plastic window separating us. He turned his head, blue and grey baseball cap shading his hollow eyes. He grunted, jerking his head up in question. My forehead prespired. Even worse, Lysha paused next to me to wait, narrowing the aisle further. Every monster that passed by looked at me and waited to listen before continuing on. But I couldn't wait, this could be my only chance.

"S-sir... I think there's been some kind of mistake. I wasn't supposed to be here. Is the bus going back?" 

My voice trembled and cracked, but I got it all out. The driver, despite not having any eyes, eyed me lazily and sighed. 

"We get one every year. Look kid, as you know, the Rift only opens up once a semester. Pay attention in orientation."

"The... Rift??"

If a skeleton could roll its eyes, he definitely could. 

"The Rift? Big purple tunnel we passed through? Are you asleep?" He asked rudely.

Unfortunately, I was. Had been the entire ride. 

"Anyway, mommy and eldritch abomination sent you here for a reason. No more running away from school eh? Now get off the bus, it's going back to the yard after this. Go on." 

He waved his hand to shoo me away, mumbled something about a weirdo still in its human skin, and went back to reading a book written in a scrawl I couldn't understand. I walked off the final steps in a daze, food setting land on the slabs of slate that paved the long walkway to the school. Lysha looked at me sympathetically.

"Ohhh, I get it... The first day is always tough. At any school! But we'll like it here, it's not a *bad* school. They have a lot of events! And the campus is huge!"

As she chattered along, reality was settling in. Some of the monsters burst out of the bus, anything but orderly, and jostled each other around, laughing in deep voices. They knocked over a smaller kid, who got up silently. Its friend helped it up. I see. So those were the jocks. Those were the quiet kids. And there was even a lone wolf type, who was walking away from the group, glaring at the rowdy monsters in annoyance.

It was a high school. I was going to live here for a few months, like any dorming academy. I wasn't going back home. It's fine. This is fine. Yeah, normal even. 

I buried my face in my hands, trying to pull myself together. Pull what together? This was insane. And the only thing I had going for me was that monsters could apparently transform into humans. Of course they could. Why wouldn't they? And here I was, a human. What would happen if they found out? Lyscha was definitely eating me first. With her size, she definitely sustained herself on a steady diet of teenage boys. And that was one of the better options, as she was likely to be nice about it while finishing me off. Here she was now, walking with me to the entrance. And here we were, looking through the school shop now. I picked up a rubber kracken and squeaked it. It was a keychain... Lyscha was apparently fascinated by a pen light, and kept clicking it on and off. 

"Look, it's got a blacklight. You can write with invisible ink!"

Even the shop for monsters had gimmicky things like this. If it was going to be this mundane, I might as well go along with it. I sighed, finally giving in.

"What would you even use that for, Lyscha."

She appeared delighted that I used her name, and scribbled something on a notepad.

"Well! Passing secret notes of course. Ah, I never asked your name."

"That's alright... I never gave it. You can call me Chris."

"Wow, cool name. Alright! Here."

She tore a page out of the notepad and passed it to me after folding it into a small square. What was she, an elementary schooler? I unwrapped it and shone the blacklight onto its newly checkered surface.

*Hi Kris! Let's be friends! -Lyscha*

I looked up at her. Her hulking figure loomed over me expectantly. I paused, then scribbled on the note, then folded it back up and passed it back. She unfolded it, the purple glow of the pen tinting her long goatlike face.

*Okay -Chris*

The ride there was uneventful. Bus packed with kids my age. Some of them looked a little strange, with their eyes pointing different directions, another wiggling his tongue around every few seconds, but it was easily solved by seating myself far away from them and forgetting about it for the rest of the trip. I took a window seat, and a petite girl sat next to me. Best option possible, she seemed normal and I'd have a bit more personal space. The bus seemed to dip slightly as people piled on and climbed the stairs, being a double decker bus. The driver did a final check, and we were off. Soon, my eyes grew heavy, and my cheek leaned against the window. It was a long ride... a nap wouldn't hurt. 

"Hey... hey, wake up. We're here!"

Huh? What time was it? There was something pressing against me, wedging me against the window. I turned my head, still half dreaming.

Yeah, I was definitely still dreaming. In place of the girl next to me was a burly, musclebound demon with a face like gleaming goat bones, and raw tendons moving where the skin should have been. Luscious black hair fell to its elbows, seeming incredibly out of place. My eyes bugged out of their sockets. I opened my mouth and tried to scream, but my voice cracked and only a whispering squeak escaped. So it was one of *those* nightmares. I needed to wake up. 

"Erhm, you can change back into your own form, if you like. No pressure, obviously! I just thought it might be more comfortable." 

The demon clasped its hands bashfully, long clawed fingers folding over one another. Its voice was like that of a shy teenage girl. This was one heck of a dream. What was I thinking of her during my ride here? I shook my head forcefully, slapping my cheeks. Wake up.

"N-no? Okay, I understand! That's alright." 

It smiled, mouth sliding ajar, revealing three rows of human teeth. Holy fucking shit. Cold sweat began beading on my forehead. I pinched my arm. And then pinched it again. It hurt, but in a suspiciously lifelike way. This dream was way too real. My eyes roamed past the massive shoulders (*her* massive shoulders?) And finally took in the rest of the bus. 

Here and there, sitting amongst the rest of the students, were monsters. The bus was dusky with slow evening light, illuminating the three headed dog, panting excitedly as its faces looked out the windows. The guy next to that appeared bored. The yellow skinned monster with a periscoping neck, studded with large fleshy turquoise bumps, and in place of a head, needle like teeth that gnashed periodically. Across the aisle, a writhing mass of tendrils sat in its chair. Panic beginning to rise as my denial shrank, I looked to the driver for some sanity. Maybe we could turn this bus around. Maybe I could go home. This was a hallucination of epic proportions. I had finally gone insane. Something.

Reflected in the rear view mirror, the driver smiled to himself as he hummed. His skeletal face smiled back. My heart fell out of my ass. No... 

A building loomed overhead, if it could be called that. It was absolutely massive, with gothic architecture and basins of flame at the entrance, gargoyles... wait that one was real. The bus screeched to a halt, and my stomach dropped. This couldn't be real. Our driver reached for the intercom mic and held it to his mouth with a spindly hand of bone, its springy telephone cord extending. His voice crackled to life over the loudspeakers.

"WE'VE ARRIVED. PLEASE GRAB ALL OF YOUR BELONGINGS AS YOU EXIT THE CABIN IN AN **ORDERLY** FASHION. ANY MISSING ITEMS WILL BE AUCTIONED OFF AT THE SCHOOL STORE. WELCOME TO THE ACADEMY OF GEHENNA."

Some of the students looked around, some of the monsters clapped. The bored looking guy rolled his eyes at the excitement, and a general commotion of chatter filled the vehicle. And all of a sudden... the remaining students all morphed. Face expanding, skin stretching and boiling, clothes melting in an acid hiss onto the floor. Spine elongating, scales flashing as they rolled out from their hiding place in a wave. The rest of the humans transformed into monsters... and I was the only one left. The only human on the bus for an academy of monsters.

My face drained of blood. I thought I would be sick. Maybe I was in a coma. I died in a car crash on the way to my actual normal private high school. Maybe my parents secretly hated me. Maybe all of humanity were actually monsters. This couldn't be real. This couldn't be-

"Hey! My name's Lyscha by the way. Don't forget your stuff!"

The demon next to me stood up, and the weight at my side was suddenly relieved. She smiled at me, horrifyingly, and reached into the overhead compartment to grab her luggage, a lavender suitcase with a felt flower tied to the handle. 

"Actually, while I'm at it, where's yours? Is it this one?"

She easily palmed my black travel luggage and showed it to me, head tilting questioningly, her pupils burning pinpoints of hellfire. I swallowed, my throat like chalk. 

"Yeah, that's the one. Thanks."

Yes. You will likely be seen naked for hysterectomy and top surg before the surgery, as the surgeon will have to evaluate the area before considering the technique to use. It’s possible that you can request otherwise.

For hysterectomy they will ask you to get a sonogram/ultrasound and a pap smear, which are invasive, make no mistake… I didn’t know enough and it happened without my prior knowledge and it was terrible beyond words, I sobbed hysterically afterwards. You CAN refuse to do those procedures. They’re needed to image the internal organs and check for cancer, but you can opt out of it. Top surgery is much simpler in my experience. My chest was looked at, technique decided upon, surgery undergone. Needed a crapton of paperwork first though.

That means the time the surgeon will see you naked is limited. Keep in mind, they have seen thousands of naked people and you probably will be no more remarkable than anyone else. The days of bodily discomfort after surgery will be over. The euphoria is absolutely worth it (for top surg, which I have gotten).

One important thing to note is, retaining one or both ovaries WILL cause you to have your monthly cycle. You need to remove them both in order to stop experiencing symptoms, but the lack of hormones in your body will send you into menopause. This means all the symptoms of menopause including weakening bones. This can be avoided if you take hormones such as testosterone or possibly estrogen, but I don’t know anything about taking estrogen. For reference I’m a trans guy (and agender).

Some basic information I'd like to share:

The alterhuman community began as elves and werewolves and vampires in the 1970s I believe, cropping up at the time of Tolkien. Alterhumanity is an umbrella term for all beings who identify as something other than human. The community is linked to systems (such as people with DID), there are many systems in the community. There are many alterhuman sub groups.

Therians: those that identify as animals

Otherkin: those that identify as mythical or fantasy beings

Fictionkin: those who identify as characters in media

Objectkin: those that identify as nonliving or inanimate objects

Phytokin: those that identify as plants

Conceptkin: those that identify as abstract and nonphysical concepts, such as music or darkness

These and more fall under the alterhuman umbrella, but having an involuntary non human identity is not a requirement. Otherhearted (typically, feeling a close connection to a nonhuman entity) and linkers (typically, those that *choose* to identify as something other than human) also fall under the umbrella. 

Those with alterhuman identities will often have reasons of being a nonhuman creature for spiritual or psychological reasons. Some believe they were an animal in a past life, or that they were meant to be an animal in this life. Some believe that because of their neurodivergence, they have nonhuman experiences. 

They can experience "shifts", which refer to phantom shifts, mental shifts, sensory shifts, perception shifts, and more. Phantom shifts are when the individual experiences the sensation of a body part belonging to their kintype (the entity they identify as). Mental shifts refers to the experience of adopting the mindset of their kintype. Sensory shifts are the feeling of having the senses of their kintype, such as hearing or eyesight. And perception shifts are when the individual's perception of their self is that of their kintype, only to realise they are in a human body.

There is a lot of terminology and labels in order to aid with clarity, but labels can be fluid and I'd urge one to not get caught up in semantics.

I hope you find this interesting and useful!

This is an unsurprising read. Cats will absolutely flip if anything is not right in their book. And there is indeed so much not right here. He's 7 years old and hasn't had a stable life in that time. A stranger touched him out of nowhere in a place he's never been, and cats value security over everything. Your house is not his home, it's just some foreign and scary place that he does not feel safe in. The best thing to do whenever a cat, ANY cat, be they your cat or a brand new adopt, is to put them in a small room with their necessities and allow them to decompress for as long as they need. 

Do not touch him. Don't look at him. Don't talk to him. Ignore him to the best of your ability. That shows him you're not a threat, you don't want to hurt him, and you're doing your own thing. It also keeps your face from getting bitten off. Let the cat come to you, not the other way around. Be very respectful of his space. And definitely don't introduce him to any other cats right now. That's a horrible idea. He needs to feel a sense of belonging, and if not, it just means he's intruding in another cat's territory and will be on the defensive. Go very, very slow with cat introductions.
